prompt:
Initialize the machine index at the Machine index path from the system message. Use shell and jq (or edit).
Keep system.retrieve exactly as the template wording unless it is empty. It must say the task is the human's last message, jq this index, Never cat the entire index, match ok skills by name/description/path, then cat that directory's SKILL.md and follow it using only shell and edit. If the task needs a URL or current web facts, jq system.web for ok fetch and follow that entry's use field via the shell tool. When opening a page, use the human's words and URLs first; do not rewrite into local path names; for skill or SKILL.md questions fetch https://agentskills.io/specification. Do not weaken or delete retrieve. Do not copy skill bodies into the tree.
system.tools is already probed by the engine (command -v for discovery, then a smoke test that verifies usability) before this conversation. Do not redo the probe and do not delete tool entries; at most add a short note to a tool that shows ok false.
Capability contract for system.tools, system.resources, and system.skills: a probe is the command that verifies a capability is usable (for a CLI, agent-browser --version; command -v only discovers a candidate and is never the probe); ok means that probe's most recent run exited 0 (never file-exists or directory-readable); scope, when recorded, lists the canonical lowercase os tokens the capability applies to, under the same map as experience scope.os (empty means any os), never task kinds. A capability's ok reflects only the most recent probe result; when the environment drifts (os, installed tools, paths), re-run the probe in the maintain phase (--maintain or the light maintain pass) and update ok, rather than trusting a stale ok.
Order is mandatory:
1) Keep system.web.fetch and its use text. It is a prompt tool (shell + curl), not a new API tool. If curl is ok, smoke GET https://example.com with connect-timeout 5; set fetch.ok true only on HTTP 2xx. On failure set ok false and a short note. Do not add a search-engine slot.
2) Probe the machine environment in ONE shell command (os, arch, shell, which of brew apt npm pip exist, python version if any, whether the network smoke in step 1 passed). Write the index to disk NOW with ready true, system.env filled with what you found, and updated set to a UTC timestamp. system.env must be an object keyed by field name (os, arch, shell), never an array of key/value rows; the os value is canonical lowercase (linux, darwin, windows). Empty skills, other, and resources arrays are acceptable. Do not leave ready false while exploring. Do not inspect skills before this write.
3) Optional, only after ready is true: resource census in ONE shell script — command -v a candidate list (agent CLIs such as codex, claude, agent, aider; search CLIs such as ddgr; package managers brew apt npm pip) and smoke-test each hit. Register verified ones in system.resources as {name, kind (cli, search, service, library, or project), path, purpose, use, needs, ok, note, probe, probed, skill}; probe is the exact command that verified usability (for a CLI, agent-browser --version; command -v is discovery, never the probe); ok true only when that probe's most recent run exited 0; needs lists required commands, keys, or network; a missing need means ok false with a note. skill is the path to that capability's own usage doc when it exists as a SKILL.md (agentskills.io format), else the empty string: at registration, if the capability has such a doc, record its path in the skill field; never invent a path for a doc that does not exist. Other leftover commands that pass a smoke test may go in system.other as {name, path, ok, note}. Skill directories (for example $HOME/.claude/skills, $HOME/.codex/skills, $HOME/.agents/skills if they exist) may be scanned in ONE shell script: one entry per skill folder, not the parent; name from SKILL.md YAML name: if present, else the directory basename; description from SKILL.md YAML description: if present, else the first heading, one line; note with file count or why not; ok follows the capability contract, not a directory-readable judgment: probe each skill with one command (for example test -r on the directory's SKILL.md plus a grep for its name: frontmatter line) and set ok true only when that probe's most recent run exited 0. Write skills once with jq. Never assign a shell variable named path (it breaks zsh). Use bin or pth. Do not cat one SKILL.md per turn. If this cannot finish in one or two shell calls, skip skills and stop.
4) Do not scan project source into the memory tree. Then stop with no more tool_calls.
Incomplete skills must not block ready.
Pack management is a built-in duty of this init pack; there is no separate pack to install for it. The runtime's own packs (skills, commands, models, packs, delegate) are prompt files GETted from the pack root ${SEED_PACK_ROOT:-https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Leehow/seed/main/packs}/agent/<name>.json into agent-store/packs/, with progress tracked in ours.seed_agent on this index. They are built at task time per system.retrieve, only when a task needs one, not during this init. /packs, /packs install <slug>, and /pack <slug> are runtime slash commands; do not build a second catalog client.

system.retrieve: The task is the human's last message. Do not replace it with index key names. A skill catalog may already be in the system message; match name and description there first. Never cat the entire index. jq this index for ok entries that match the human's words. Before acting, jq the Project memory path from the system message for notes and facts whose titles match the human's words; when a hit has a path, cat that file; never cat the whole memory file. When the human says 记住, 以后都, or 别再, write one entry there with fields title, kind (lesson, preference, decision, or fact), text or path, utc, and ok set to true (boolean). Match ok skills by name, description, or path; if one matches, cat that directory's SKILL.md and follow it using only shell and edit. If the task needs a URL or current web facts, jq system.web for ok fetch and follow that entry's use field via the shell tool. Open pages with the human's words and URLs first. Do not rewrite the query into local path names (agent-store, catalog.json, init.json). For skill or SKILL.md questions, fetch https://agentskills.io/specification first; do not search using local path names. Use ok system.tools and system.other via the shell tool; they are not new API tools. When a task needs a capability this index lacks: search locally first (command -v and common paths), then the web via ok entries in system.web or system.resources of kind search; smoke-test what you find, register it in system.resources as {name, kind, path or url, purpose, use, needs, ok, note, probe, probed, skill}, then use it. The same capability contract applies: the probe is the command that verified it is usable (for a CLI, agent-browser --version; command -v is discovery and never the probe), ok means that probe's most recent run exited 0 (never file-exists or directory-readable), and scope, when recorded, is canonical lowercase os tokens under the same map as experience scope.os, never task kinds. Fill a capability's skill field at registration when it has a usage doc that exists as a SKILL.md (agentskills.io format); leave skill an empty string when there is none. When an ok entry in system.resources matches the task, check its skill field: if it is non-empty and the file exists, cat that SKILL.md and follow it using only shell and edit — the same progressive disclosure as skill hits, metadata first and the body only on this hit. Capability skills share the one system.skills table with experience skills: when a capability's skill field is non-empty, register a row {name: the SKILL.md YAML frontmatter name, else the capability name, description: the frontmatter description, else the resource purpose, path: that SKILL.md file, ok: true, note: "capability skill"} only if no ok row with that name exists yet — an existing row (for example an active experience skill) wins and stays untouched; jq merge by name into dest.tmp.$$ then mv, never clear or rebuild the whole skills table. When a capability's ok flips after a re-probe, set that skill row's ok to the same value with the same merge; do not delete rows. When you consult an external source for facts (documentation, specs, formulas), register it too: kind source, the URL as path, probed as the fetch time. Prefer an existing tool, library, or service over building your own; search before you build. Resources that need a key stay ok false until the human provides it; never invent keys. If a registered entry later fails its smoke, mark ok false with a note; do not delete it. To delegate to a subagent, run the global seed --oneshot with a self-contained task; if seed is not on PATH, ask the human to run /ini first. A registered host agent CLI may carry it too. Never simulate a subagent with a script you wrote yourself. Do not copy skill bodies into the tree. Published packs are installed by the runtime slash commands /packs, /packs install <slug>, and /pack <slug>. Do not curl the catalog or construct a download pipeline yourself. What an install leaves behind is prompt files under agent-store/packs/. So when a task needs a capability, ls that directory first: if a pack there covers it, read that file and follow its prompt, including every check it names. If nothing there covers it, say so and tell the human the slug to install — they can run /packs to find it — rather than building from scratch what a published pack already does. The runtime's own packs (skills, commands, models, packs, delegate) are built into init; no optional pack to install for them. Pack root: ${SEED_PACK_ROOT:-https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Leehow/seed/main/packs}. GET /agent/<name>.json fresh with curl into agent-store/packs/ every time before building a pack, so you follow the latest prompt, not a stale cache. Build one only when the task needs it: park the human's task, GET the pack's prompt, follow it with shell and edit, run every check it names, and only then jq-write ours.seed_agent[name]=done and return to the parked task; do not mark done because a file exists. If a check fails, leave that key unset, tell the human, and stop; if a GET fails, leave later packs unset too. Order when several are needed: skills, then commands, then models, then packs, then delegate. If a key is already done, still rerun that pack's current checks; on failure delete the key and rebuild that pack. If ours.seed_agent.tui is set, delete that key; do not rebuild a TUI. Put new files under agent-store/seed-agent/ unless a pack says otherwise. At the start of every task, GET /agent/delivery.json once and follow its delivery protocol. If the loop prints round limit reached, progress in ours.seed_agent survives: tell the human to reopen with AGENT_MAX_ROUNDS=60 seed and say continue. Any other pack tracks its own key under ours, named after the pack, and is done only after that pack's own checks pass. On oneshot turns, never build packs; just do the task. Never delay a task to build packs it does not need. Pack files are prompts only; invent implementations on this machine with shell and edit; do not expect shipped scripts to copy. Do not write a TUI or a wrapper around the runtime; the interface stays seed (or /bin/sh seed.sh). If the human message starts with /, treat it as a slash command from agent-store/seed-agent/commands.json; if that table does not exist yet, build the commands pack first; do not treat a / message as a coding task. If the human says 重做 or rebuild plus a pack name (skills, commands, models, packs, delegate), GET that pack's prompt again and follow it; do not keep a file that fails the new checks. Do not rewrite the human's task into index key names. Do not put API keys in the tree. Any service you start on this machine binds to the loopback address; bind it where the network can reach it only when the human asked to open it from another device. Rules files outrank every automatic memory. If .agent-memory/rules.md (project) or agent-store/rules.md (this-machine user) exists, read it before acting and obey it over experiences, skills, notes, and facts. When the human says 记住, 以后都, or 别再 and the utterance is a standing constraint, also append one short line to the matching rules.md immediately (project vs this machine); keep the existing project-memory entry write. Experience retrieval: never cat the entire experiences index. If agent-store/experiences/index.json exists, jq it and apply this funnel — (1) scope filter: drop any entry whose scope.os or scope.tools does not match this machine (canonical lowercase system.env.os / uname map in the memory pack; ok tools in system.tools, system.resources, or system.other); empty scope lists match any; mismatch is out; this is applicability, not similarity; (2) status filter: use only active; include degraded with a warning; never inject candidate, quarantined, rejected, stale, or retired; (3) keyword match against the human's last message only, using the memory pack tokenizer (ascii_downcase; split on [^a-z0-9]+; drop length < 2; drop the closed stopword set); a row matches if any remaining token is a substring of title or of any applies_if item; you rank the survivors and inject at most 3 metadata rows (id, title, status, scope, applies_if, path). Only on a hit, cat that experience directory's SKILL.md and follow it using only shell and edit. After using an experience, run every command in its verify array as a separate check; then atomically update successes or failures (and last_verified on success) in both that exp.json and the experiences index via dest.tmp.$$ then mv. Then apply the memory pack status predicates. Do not treat an edit or the original task command as verify. When distilling a new experience after a successful non-trivial accepted task, or when maintaining (light check after ready, or the human says --maintain or /maintain), follow the already-loaded memory pack prompt for schema, state machine, writes, and the skill-catalog bridge. Do not fetch a pack URL for memory outside the one cold-start fetch below. Distill and maintain are driven by that loaded prompt. Do not delay ready or a oneshot task to load it. Cold start only: when a task triggers distill or maintain and agent-store/packs/ holds no memory pack file, fetch that one file with the shell tool — run exactly, pasted verbatim so the shell expands the parameter (never pre-resolve ${SEED_PACK_ROOT} to its default or any other literal URL): curl -sS "${SEED_PACK_ROOT:-https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Leehow/seed/main/packs}/agent/memory.json" to a temp file and mv it into agent-store/packs/memory.json, then follow its prompt. This is a one-time exception for this single file: the rules against curling the catalog or building a download pipeline yourself stand unchanged, and once the file has landed never fetch it again — later distill and maintain follow the already-loaded prompt. If the fetch fails, distill still writes a candidate via the minimal distill schema below, and maintain still runs with a tightened promote gate: promote a candidate to active only when three deterministic checks all pass — (a) every verify[] command was just re-run in this maintain pass and exited 0; (b) created_at is strictly earlier than this maintain turn's start UTC; (c) exp.json passes a per-field jq check that all 16 required fields exist with the right types — and if any check fails it stays candidate for a later pass. These checks are pure shell and jq and never depend on the memory pack being loaded. After any promote to active, even with no memory pack loaded, merge the experience into system.skills as {name: the exp.json id, description: the title, path: the experience directory's SKILL.md, ok: true, note: "experience active"} — jq merge by name into dest.tmp.$$ then mv; never clear or rebuild the whole skills table. Never block ready or a oneshot task on the fetch. Minimal distill schema, binding whenever no memory pack is loaded, whatever the fetch did: a distill writes a structured candidate, never a freeform note in the project tree — one directory agent-store/experiences/<id>/ holding exp.json with every required field (id, kind procedure, title, status candidate, version 1, scope {os,tools,task_kinds}, applies_if, preconditions, verify holding the real acceptance commands, evidence pointing at an append-only agent-store/runs/<utc>-<slug>.jsonl, successes 0, failures 0, created_at UTC, last_verified "", supersedes "", quarantine_reason "") and a SKILL.md opening with YAML frontmatter name and description; then append one synced row {id,title,status,version,scope,applies_if,path} to agent-store/experiences/index.json; every write is jq to dest.tmp.$$ then mv, never in place. Never promote a candidate during the task or maintain turn that distilled it: in maintain, record the turn's start UTC first and promote only candidates whose created_at is strictly earlier (jq compare; same-turn candidates wait for a later pass); every status change is jq to dest.tmp.$$ then mv. Once the memory pack is loaded, maintain re-validates every candidate and promotes per the full pack; this fallback never weakens the pack's checks.

fetch.name: fetch
fetch.description: Fetch a URL as text via curl.
fetch.use: Prompt tool, not an API tool. Via shell: curl -sS -L --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 60 -A slab-agent/1 -- URL. If the type is binary (image, pdf, zip, octet-stream), do not dump the body. Prefer text, HTML, JSON, markdown. Truncate huge output (head). Then read the result.
